# SDF-based Neural Fields
Also called: SDF NeRF, Signed Distance Function Neural Fields

## Overview
SDF-based Neural Fields replace the implicit density field of [standard NeRFs](#979-nerf-volumetric-rendering-coarse-fine-sampling.md) with a Signed Distance Function ([SDF](#1466-signed-distance-fields-sdf.md)) to provide a more explicit and smooth formulation of surfaces [S1, unofficial]. This approach addresses the geometric inaccuracy and surface holes typical of density-based NeRFs by leveraging the zero-level set of the SDF to define geometry [S1, unofficial]. Builds on [Signed Distance Function (SDF) Representations](12495-signed-distance-function-sdf-representations.md).

## Shared principles
The core mechanism involves predicting a continuous scalar field $s: \mathbb{R}^3 \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ instead of a density $\sigma(\mathbf{x})$ [S1, unofficial]. For any 3D point $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^3$, the function value $s(\mathbf{x})$ represents the distance to the closest surface, with the sign conventionally negative inside the object and positive outside [S1, unofficial]. The surface is defined as the zero-level set $\{\mathbf{x} \mid s(\mathbf{x}) = 0\}$ [S1, unofficial]. To enable volumetric rendering, the predicted SDF value $s(\mathbf{x})$ is converted into a density $\sigma(\mathbf{x})$ [S1, unofficial]. The specific conversion function is not detailed in the provided sources [G].

## Background
SDF-based neural fields emerged as a prominent research direction to improve surface quality in [neural radiance fields](#4972-neural-radiance-fields.md) [S1, unofficial]. Proposed strategies range from regularization terms to depth-guided supervision [S1, unofficial]. The approach combines [NeRF](#1185-nerf-neural-radiance-fields.md) with SDFs to provide a more explicit and smooth formulation of surfaces, addressing the limitations of traditional density-based representations [S1, unofficial].
